name: Compassion UK child sponsorship (SoGive, 2020)
summary: Sponsors children in poor countries through church-run centres that pay for schooling, health care and meals. SoGive's estimate of the cost per year of extra income that sponsorship's extra schooling brings, rebuilt from SoGive's analysis.

source.title: Compassion UK Christian Child Development: SoGive rating and analysis
source.license: No licence on the page. SoGive's data terms (sogive.org/doc/getourdata.html, archived September 2019): data for charity analysis is free with attribution to SoGive; use in apps needs a licence, free for low-intensity use, on condition that users are told the source of impact assessments with a link back to SoGive. This model cites SoGive and links its page.

resources.title: SoGive, Compassion UK analysis
resources.note: SoGive's charity page (its analysis text); SoGive publishes no spreadsheet for it, so the model is built from the figures stated in the text, each quoted on its row. Rated "Not Recommended (firm)"; the record was last modified on 11 November 2020.

resources.title: Wydick, Glewwe & Rutledge (2013), Does international child sponsorship work? A six-country study of impacts on adult life outcomes, Journal of Political Economy 121(2)

sections.title: From pounds per year of extra income to value per dollar
sections.explainer: charityevals' steps after SoGive's bottom line: SoGive adds up years of income linearly; the site values income in logarithms, as GiveWell does, and discounts it over the years until the sponsored child starts work and through a working life. Then pounds to dollars.

sections.title: Staff pay below market
sections.explainer: charityevals' step, not the evaluator's: with credit by share of resources on, staff's pay below what they could earn elsewhere counts as an in-kind contribution and gets its share of the outcome. Off by default.

rows.label: Extra years of schooling from sponsorship
rows.explainer: Wydick, Glewwe and Rutledge (2013), a six-country study of Compassion's sponsorship programme, found 1 to 1.5 more years of schooling; SoGive takes the top of the range.

rows.label: Income gain from each extra year of schooling

source.title: SoGive, charity analysis
source.quote: If we take the World Bank's estimate that an additional year's schooling increase incomes by about 10%

rows.label: Years of additional income per sponsored child
rows.explainer: SoGive: "a typical beneficiary would receive the equivalent of six years' additional income (0.1*1.5*40 years)": a 15% higher income for 40 years, added up as six years of a whole income.

rows.label: Cost of a sponsorship (£)

source.title: SoGive, charity analysis
source.quote: As the average sponsored child received around £3,000 of support

rows.explainer: The average sponsorship in the study lasted 9.3 years.

rows.label: Cost per year of additional income (£)
rows.explainer: SoGive: "this means it costs Compassion £500 to provide someone with an additional year's income", against its benchmark of £50 to double someone's income for a year. SoGive also tries a generous allowance for health benefits (preventing all deaths at ages 5–14 at Ugandan rates, 0.014 lives per sponsorship) and finds it doesn't change the verdict; that allowance isn't in this figure.

rows.label: Log-income gain per year of additional income
rows.explainer: SoGive counts a 15% gain for 40 years as six whole years of income. The site values income on a log scale, as GiveWell does: a 15% gain a year is ln(1.15) = 0.14 of log income, 0.20 of a doubling, so each of SoGive's years of income (0.15 of a year's income ÷ 0.15) is worth 0.93 of log income, 1.34 doublings.

rows.label: Discount rate on future income
rows.explainer: The shared discount rate (Your values). SoGive doesn't discount, so the evaluator view pins it at 0.

rows.label: Years from the average pound spent until the extra earnings start
rows.explainer: Our judgment: sponsorship runs through school (9.3 years on average), so the average pound is spent about halfway through, some 5 to 6 years before the child starts work.

rows.label: Discount factor for the timing of the extra earnings
US dollars per pound, 2020
rows.explainer: charityevals' step: SoGive's figure is in pounds; the site counts per dollar, so the pounds are converted at the year's average exchange rate (shared fact).

rows.label: Units of value per dollar
rows.explainer: Years of additional income per dollar, in log income, valued at the site's value of a unit of log income (Your values), discounted for timing.

rows.label: Staff pay as a share of program cost
rows.explainer: Default for programs where staff deliver the help themselves (treatment, counselling, coaching, outreach): staff pay is about half the cost. Our judgment; we haven't seen this program's breakdown.

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable jobs elsewhere
rows.explainer: Health workers and field staff at nonprofits often earn somewhat less than in comparable jobs. Our judgment.

rows.label: Salary forgone by staff per dollar of cost (in-kind donation)
Share of the full cost paid in cash
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, staff's forgone pay counts as part of the cost, and staff get their share of the outcome. Off, this is 100%.

rows.label: Units of value per dollar donated
rows.explainer: The figure per dollar above; with credit by share of resources, times the share of the full cost paid in cash (staff's forgone pay is the rest).
